texts.facts: Petitioners have filed the present writ petition under Article 226 of the Constitution of India seeking quashment of the proceedings of case No.23/2016, the report of the Food Analyst dated 26.09.2015, the orders dated 17.06.2016 and 25.06.2016 and. Facts of the case, in short, are as under: 2. Petitioners No.1 to 4 are the Directors of Firm Parle Agro Pvt. Ltd. (respondent No.7) and petitioner No.5 is the Executive Chairman of petitioner No.7. Petitioner No.6 is the nominee of petitioner No.7 under the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 (for short 'the Act of 2006'). 3. Respondent No.1 is the Food Safety Officer under the Act of 2006, respondents No.2 & 3 are adjudicating and designated officers under the Act of 2006. 4. That on 8.9.2015 the Food Safety Officer, district Dhar purchased a sample of mango drink "Frooti" from Hotel Vrindavan at village Dasai, Tehsil Sardarpur, district Dhar for analysis. The sample was taken in the shape of a bottle with a quantity of 600 ml. After taking the sample he prepared a memorandum in Form Mr. Ashok Bhaves vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 9 September, 2019 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/130631743/ 1 No.VI and dispatched to the Food Analyst on 09.09.2015 by registered post. The details of Food sample mentioned in the Form VI are as under (i) Batch No. is BHP008, (ii) Packed on 26.04.2015 and (iii) best for use within six months. 5. Vide letter dated 28.10.2015 the Food Safety Officer informed the Manager/Director of Parle Agro Pvt. Ltd., Mandideep that a sample of Frooti mango drink was taken on 08.09.2015 which has been sent to Food Analyst and also directed them to provide the details about the name of proprietor of the firm, name of Directors of the firm, name of the nominee, if any, certified copy of the food license, annual turn over the firm, memorandum of article and certified copy of the ITR. 6. Vide letter dated 23.12.2015 the prescribed authority supplied the food analysis report given by the Food Analyst in Form VII-A dated 08.09.2015 to the proprietor of Hotel Vrindavan and Manager/Director of Parle Agro Pvt. Ltd., Mandideep & Mumbai so that they may prefer an appeal under section 46 (4) of the Act of 2006 and rule 2.4.6 of the Food Safety and Standards Rules, 2011 (for short 'the Rules of 2011'), however, the petitioners, did not prefer any appeal under the aforesaid provision. Vide letters dated 23.02.2016 & 24.03.2016 the Food Safety Officer sought various information i.e. the name of proprietor of the firm, name of Directors of the firm, name of the nominee, if any, certified copy of the food license, annual turn over the firm, memorandum of article and certified copy of the ITR from the petitioners. Vide letter dated 12.04.2016 the petitioners supplied the information to the office of the Joint Commissioner, Food & Drug Administration, Dhar. 7. Vide letter dated 17.06.2016 the Food Safety Officer, Dhar sought permission under section 36 (3)(e) of the Act of 2006 from the prescribed authority to launch prosecution against the petitioners. Vide order dated 17.06.2016 the prescribed authority has granted the permission to prosecute the petitioners and others under sections 26(1), (2)(ii) read with section 51 of the Act of 2006. After obtaining the aforesaid permission the Food Safety Officer filed a written complaint before the adjudicating authority. Vide order dated 25.06.2016 the adjudicating authority / the Additional District Magistrate; Dhar has registered a case against the petitioners and issued a show-cause notice for an appearance on 29.07.2016. Being aggrieved by the aforesaid order of sanction for prosecution and show cause notice the petitioners have approached this Court by way of the writ petition. By order dated 06.04.2017 this Court issued show- cause notice to the respondents and by way of interim relief the further proceedings in pursuance to the impugned order dated 25.06.2016 pending before the adjudicating officer has been stayed. 8. Petitioners have assailed the impugned action of the respondents mainly on the ground that the report of the Food Analyst was communicated to them vide letter dated 23.12.2015 which was received by them on 02.01.2016 nevertheless by that time the shelf life of the sample produce had already been expired, therefore, they have been denied statutory right to prefer the appeal under section 46 (4) before the designated officer for forwarding one part of the sample to the referral lab, Mr. Ashok Bhaves vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 9 September, 2019 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/130631743/ 2 hence now they cannot be prosecuted for violation of the provisions of the Act and the entire proceedings vitiates are liable to the [LEAKAGE_MASK]. 9. After notice respondents have filed the return by submitting that the Food Safety Officer collected the sample on 08.09.2015 and sent the sample for testing to the Food Analyst. The Food Analyst submitted a report under section 46 of the Act of 2006 on 26.09.2015 i.e. before the expiry of shelf life of the sample. The information along with the copy of the report was sent to the petitioners but they did not choose to prefer any appeal under section 46(4) of the Act of 2006. As per the report of the Food Analyst, the product was found sub-standard, hence based on the Food Analyst's report sanction for prosecution has rightly been granted against the petitioner. Initially, the petitioner/company had sent the name of Manish Kumar as nominee but later on, they changed the nominee without informing the licensing authority, hence the sanction has been granted for prosecution against the petitioners. The petitioners are free to raise all objections before the adjudicating officer and thereafter they have a remedy before the Tribunal which has been notified by gazette notification dated 25.10.2013 and 30.08.2013, hence the present petition is liable to be dismissed.
texts.arguments: It is further submitted that section 66 of the Act of 2006 provides offences by companies and according to which every person who at the time the offence was committed was in charge of and was responsible to the company for the conduct of the business of the company shall be prosecuted. 10. Shri Aniket A. Naik, learned counsel appearing for the petitioners argued that the sample was taken on 08.09.2015 wherein the packaging date is mentioned as 26.04.2015 with a condition "best before six month" hence shelf life of the food product was only six months and the Food Analyst submitted its report on 26.09.2015 which was sent to the petitioners on 23.12.2015 i.e. after expiry of shelf life of the sample on 26.10.2015, therefore, the petitioners could not exercise their statutory right of appeal before the designated officer seeking referral of the sample to the referral lab, therefore, they cannot be prosecuted on the basis of the Food Analyst's report alone and the entire proceedings initiated against the petitioners are now futility, hence liable to be [LEAKAGE_MASK]. In support of his contention he has placed reliance over the judgments passed by the Apex Court in the case of Gupta Chemicals Pvt. Ltd. & others vs. State of Rajasthan and another (2010) 7 SCC 735; Municipal Corporation of Delhi vs. Ghisa Ram AIR 1967 SC 970; Rajkumar Tinker vs. Food Inspector 2016 SCC OnLine MP 5089 and the judgment of this Court in the case of Prahlad Gattani & others vs. State of M.P ILR (2012) MP 1454. 11. Per contra, Shri Arvind Sharma learned Govt. Advocate appearing for the respondents submitted that the sample was found to be sub-standard and the petitioners did not prefer any appeal despite receipt of information and assumed that the appeal cannot be preferred as the shelf life of the product had expired. It is for the appellate authority to decide as to whether the product can be tested or not after the expiry period. The prosecution can be launched against the petitioners based on the Food Analyst's report even if no appeal has been preferred. The entire petition is based on the surmises and conjecture that the entire proceeding before the adjudicating authority is in futility in absence of any appeal to the designated officer. Under section 3(h) "designated Officer" means the officer appointed under section 36. Under section 3(i) "Food Analyst" means an analyst appointed under section 45. As per section 3 (n) "food business" means any undertaking, whether for profit or not and whether public or private, carrying out any of the activities related to any stage of manufacture, processing, packaging, storage, transportation, distribution of food, import and includes food services, catering services, sale of food or food ingredients. Under section 3 (o) "food business operator" in relation to food business is a person by whom the business is carried on or owned and is responsible for ensuring the compliance of this Act, rules and regulations made thereunder. As per section 3(p) "food laboratory" means any food laboratory or institute established by the Central or a State Government or any other agency and accredited by National Accreditation Board for Testing and Calibration Laboratories or an equivalent accreditation agency and recognized by the Food Authority under section 43. Under section 3 (zx) "sub- standard" an article of food shall be deemed to be sub- standard if it does not meet the specified standards but not so as to render the article of food unsafe and under section 3(zz) "unsafe food" means an article of food whose nature, substance or quality is so affected as to render it injurious to health. 14. Section 26 defines the responsibilities of the food business operator and section 27 provides the liability of manufacturers, packers, wholesalers, distributors and sellers. Under section 42 the Food Safety Officer shall be responsible for inspection of food business, drawing samples and sending them to Food Analyst. Under subsection (2) of section 42, the Food Analyst after receiving the sample from the Food Safety Officer shall analyse the sample and send the analysis report mentioning the method of sampling and analysis within fourteen days to the designated officer for sanction. Under section (3) of section 42, the designated officer after scrutiny of the report of Food Analyst shall decide as to whether the contravention is punishable with imprisonment or fine only. In case he finds that the contravention is punishable with imprisonment, he shall send his recommendation within fourteen days to the Commissioner of Food Safety for sanctioning prosecution. Under subsection (4) of section 42, the Commissioner of Food Safety shall, if he so deems fit, as per the gravity of the offence, may refer the matter either to a Court of ordinary jurisdiction or to a special Court. If the designated officer decides that the Mr. Ashok Bhaves vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 9 September, 2019 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/130631743/ 4 contravention is not punishable with imprisonment but only with fine under the provisions of the Act, he shall cause and authorize the Food Safety Officer to file an application before the Adjudicating Officer for adjudication of the offence against the person who alleged to have committed the offence. Under sub-section (1) of section 46 on receipt of a package containing a sample for analysis from a Food Safety Officer the Food Analyst shall examine the seal and thereafter cause to analyse such sample of an article of food within a period of fourteen days from the date of receipt of the sample and send the report. Subsection (4) of section 46 provides an appeal against the report of Food Analyst before the designated officer who shall if he so decides, refers the matter to the referral food laboratory. For the sake of convenience sections 46 & 47 are reproduced below: 46.Functions of Food Analyst.-(1)On receipt of a package containing a sample for analysis from a Food Safety Officer or any other person , the Food Analyst shall compare the seal on the container and the outer cover with specimen impression received separately and shall note the conditions of the seal thereon: Provided that in case a sample container received by the Food Analyst is found to be in broken condition or unfit for analysis, he shall within seven days from the date of receipt of such sample inform the Designated Officer about the same and send a requisition to him for sending the second part of the sample. (2) The Food Analyst shall cause to be analysed such samples of an article of food as may be sent to him by Food Safety Officer or by any other person authorised under this Act. (3) The Food Analyst shall, within fourteen days from the date of receipt of any sample for analysis, send-- (i) where such sample is received under section 38 or section 47, to the Designated Officer, four copies of the report indicating the method of sampling and analysis; and Mr. Ashok Bhaves vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 9 September, 2019 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/130631743/ 5 (ii) where such sample is received under section 40, a copy of the report indicating the method of sampling and analysis to the person who had purchased such article of food with a copy to the Designated Officer: Provided that in case the sample cannot be analysed within fourteen days of its receipt, the Food Analyst shall inform the Designated Officer and the Commissioner of Food Safety giving reasons and specifying the time to be taken for analysis. (4) An appeal against the report of Food Analyst shall lie before the Designated Officer who shall if he so decides, refer the matter to the referral food laboratory as notified by the Food Authority for opinion. 47. Sampling and analysis.-(1) When a Food Safety Officer takes a sample of food for analysis, he shall- (a) give notice in writing of his intention to have it so analysed to the person from whom he has taken the sample and to the person, if any, whose name, address and other particulars have been disclosed; (b) except in special cases as may be provided by rules made under this Act, divide the sample into four parts and mark and seal or fasten up each part in such a manner as its nature permits and take the signature or thumb impression of the person from whom the sample has been taken in such place and such manner as may be prescribed by the Central Government: Provided that where such person refuses to sign or put his thumb impression, the Food Safety Officer shall call upon one or more witnesses and take his signature or thumb impression, instead of the signature or thumb impression of such person; (c) (i) send one of the parts for analysis to the Food Analyst under intimation to the Designated Officer; (ii) send two parts to the Designated Officer for keeping these in safe custody; and (iii) send the remaining part for analysis to an accredited laboratory, if so requested by the food business operator, under intimation to the Designated Officer: Provided that if the test reports received under sub-clauses (i) and (iii) are found to be at variance, then the Designated Officer shall send one part of the sample kept in his custody, to referral laboratory for analysis, whose decision thereon shall be final. When a sample of any article of food or adulterant is taken, the Food Safety Officer shall, by the immediate succeeding working day, send the sample to the Food Analyst for the area concerned for analysis and report. (4) An article of food or adulterant seized, unless destroyed, shall be produced before the Designated Officer as soon as possible and in any case not later than seven days after the receipt of the report of the Food Analyst: Provided that if an application is made to the Designated Officer in this behalf by the person from whom any article of food has been seized, the Designated Officer shall by order in writing direct the Food Safety Officer to produce such article before him within such time as may be specified in the order. 1. When an appeal as provided under subsection 4 of section 46 is preferred to the Designated Officer by the Food Business Operator against the report of the Food Analyst, the Designated Officer, shall if he so decides, within thirty days from the receipt of such appeal after considering the material placed before him and after giving an opportunity to Food Business Operator to be heard shall forward one part of the sample to the referral lab. If the Designated Officer decides that such contravention is not punishable with imprisonment but only with fine under the provisions of the Act, he shall cause and authorize the Food Safety Officer to file with the Adjudicating Officer an application for adjudication of the offence alleged to have been committed by the person from whom the food sample has been taken or the person whose name and address and other particulars have been disclosed under Rule 2.5 of these rules and/or the seller or manufacturer of the food item in respect of which the report has been received. 5. The Adjudicating Officer shall have the power to hold an inquiry for purpose of adjudicating offences punishable under sections 50, 51, 52, 53, 54, 55, 56, 57, 58, 64, 65, 66 and 67 of the Act. 6. For holding an inquiry for adjudication under section 68 of the Act as to whether any person(s) has/have committed contravention of any of the provisions of the Act referred to in Rule 3.1.1. (5) herein or the rules or regulations in respect of which the offence is alleged to have been committed, the Adjudicating Officer shall, in the first instance, issue a notice to such person or persons giving him or them an opportunity to make a representation in the matter within such period as may be specified in the notice (not being less than 30 days from the date of service thereof). 7. Every notice under Rule 3.1.1.(6) to any such person shall indicate the nature of offence alleged to have been committed by him or them, the section(s) of the Act alleged to have been contravened, and the date of hearing of the matter. A copy of the report of the Food Analyst shall also be annexed to such notice. 8. On the date fixed for hearing, the Adjudicating Officer shall explain to the person or persons proceeded against or to his authorized representative, the offence alleged to have been committed by such person, indicating the provision of the Act, rules or regulations in respect of which the contravention is alleged to have taken place. 9. The Adjudicating Officer shall then allow such person or persons to produce such documents or evidence as he may consider relevant to the inquiry and if necessary the hearing may be adjourned to a future date. Provided that the notice referred to in Rule 3.1.1. (6) may, at the request of the person concerned, be waived. Provided further that the Adjudicating Officer shall pass the final order within 90 days from the date of first hearing mentioned in Rule 3.1.1 (8) above. 11. While holding an inquiry under this rule, the Adjudicating Officer shall have the power to summon and enforce the attendance of any person acquainted with the facts and circumstances of the case to give evidence or to produce any document which, in the opinion of the Adjudicating Officer may be useful for or relevant to, the subject matter of the inquiry. 21.
